title: Animal Health Australia and Plant Health Australia Funding Legislation Amendment Bill 2021
short_title: Animal Health Australia and Plant Health Australia Funding Legislation Amendment Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change how animal and plant biosecurity levies are administered and spent, including funding priorities for emergency responses and other eligible health activities.
Animal Health Australia could fund responses under additional prescribed deeds, while Plant Health Australia could use remaining emergency response funds for broader plant health purposes.
The changes would start on 1 July 2022 and also remove provisions concerning honey levies and the redirection of surplus plant levies to research bodies.
changes: The Governor-General would gain a regulation-making power under the animal health funding legislation.
The departmental secretary could recognise one or more relevant plant industry bodies through a notifiable instrument.
Plant Health Australia would receive total relevant levy and penalty receipts rather than amounts limited by annual contribution liability.
Plant levy provisions would accommodate multiple industry bodies representing the same plant product.
summary.affected: Animal Health Australia, Plant Health Australia and participating animal and plant industries would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Trevor Evans
speeches.brief: The government argued the Animal Health Australia and Plant Health Australia Funding Legislation Amendment Bill 2021 will increase efficiency, reduce red tape, and improve flexibility for industry parties in emergency biosecurity response deeds, while opposing Labor's amendment as unnecessary.
